title: Frontend: Priority Queue
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Priority Queue. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(commands). Numeric min-heap operations: {type:push,value} returns heap size, {type:pop} returns smallest or null, {type:peek} reads smallest or null. Preserve duplicates.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use array indices for parent and children.
alternativeApproaches: Support priority updates using an index map and explain why changing an item in place breaks the heap unless it is repaired.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Empty pop; one item; equal priorities.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
